Irregular Conduct Of Customs
Nippon Staff Said To Be Curbed

Warning has been served on the Japanese staff of the Chinese Maritime Customs by Commissioner L. H. Lawford in connection with the illegal boarding and search of foreign vessels, a Chinese report said yesterday.

While official confirmation of the report could not be obtained, it was learned, however, that a meeting of the Commissioner with the Japanese staff occurred last Saturday.

The report indicated that Mr. Lawford disapproved of such acts of the Japanese and recently conducted a personal investigation of charges against his staff.

At the Saturday meeting, the Japanese were reported to have been told that they must observe the rules of the Customs service. Special measures would be taken if the violations of the rules were continued, he was alleged to have said.

Regarding the illegal boarding and search of vessels, the report stated that foreign steamship companies were considering means of checking such unlawful practices.

海关的不当行为
据称日籍职员受到约束

据一份中文报告昨日称，税务司 L. H. Lawford 已就非法登临和搜查外国船只一事，向中国海关的日籍职员发出警告。

虽然无法获得该报告的官方证实，但据悉，税务司上周六与日籍职员举行了一次会议。

该报告指出，Lawford 先生不赞成日方的此类行为，并最近亲自对其职员受到的指控进行了调查。

据称，在周六的会议上，日方被告知必须遵守海关服务的规章。他还声称，如果继续违反规章，将采取特别措施。

关于非法登船和搜查船只的问题，报告称外国轮船公司正在考虑制止此类非法做法的手段。

March 3, 1939.

Reported arrest of terrorist suspect by the River Police.

With reference to the attached translation from the
"Tairiku Shimpo" dated March 2, 1939, regarding the reported
arrest of a Chinese terrorist suspect, I have to state that
a male Chinese named Fang You Be (方有培), aged 21, was
arrested by a search party belonging the River Police at 11.05
p.m. February 25, 1939, on board the s.s. Ave Maria, which
was berthed at No. 5 S.M.P. Pontoon. He was found in
possession of two packages containing pamphlets and Chinese
military uniforms, etc.,

Questioned by the River Police, Fang You Be gave his
address as Sing Sing Li (新々里), Dah Poo Jau (打浦桥),
French Concession, and was employed by the Yu Li Printing
Shop (有利印刷公司) on Rue Pere Robert for about two months,
commencing from July 1938. While in the employ of this
shop he had a friend named Yau Tsong Kyong (姚忠景), whom
he met at about 2 p.m. on February 25 on Avenue Joffree and
was requested by this friend to meet him again at Dah Poo Jau
at 8.15 p.m. the same day. The prisoner met Yau Tsong
Kyong at the appointed time and place, when he was handed
two packages and requested to take them board the s.s. Ave
Maria.

Whilst Fang was waiting aboard the vessel for Yau he
was arrested and taken to the River Police Station. Efforts
to find Y„ were unavailing.

The two bundles in question contained the following
articles:-

1 military cap and badge.
2 army leather belts.
2 pairs of shoes ( 1 canvas and 1 Chinese).
1 pair of khaki breeches.
1 pair of army putties.

报告水上警察逮捕恐怖嫌疑犯一事。

关于附件中译自1939年3月2日《大陆新报》的报道，涉及一名中国恐怖嫌疑犯被捕的消息，兹陈述如下：一名名为方有培（Fang You Be）的21岁中国男子，于1939年2月25日晚上11点05分，在停泊于工部局警务处5号浮桥的“圣母玛利亚”号轮船上，被隶属于水上警察的一个搜查队逮捕。他被发现持有两个包裹，内含宣传册和中国军服等物品。

经水上警察讯问，方有培供称其住址为法租界打浦桥（Dah Poo Jau）新新里（Sing Sing Li），自1938年7月起在罗伯特神父路（Rue Pere Robert）的有利印刷公司（Yu Li Printing Shop）受雇约两个月。在该店任职期间，他有一位名叫姚忠景（Yau Tsong Kyong）的朋友，他于2月25日下午2点左右在霞飞路（Avenue Joffree）与该朋友相遇，并被该朋友要求于当晚8点15分再次在打浦桥见面。囚犯在指定时间和地点与姚忠景会面，当时他接过两个包裹，并被要求将它们带上“圣母玛利亚”号轮船。

当方在船上等待姚时，他被逮捕并带往水上警察局。寻找姚的努力未果。

这两个包裹中包含以下物品：-

1顶军帽及帽徽。
2条军用皮带。
2双鞋（1双帆布鞋和1双中式鞋）。
1条卡其色马裤。
1副军用绑腿。

TERRORIST ARRESTED
BY RIVER POLICE

Instructions From Gen.
Chiang Said Found
On Prisoner

Into the dragnet against terrorists
spread by the River Police of the
Shanghai Maritime Customs ran an
unnamed Chinese youth on Wednes-
day night as he was about to land
from an unidentified Portuguese
vessel, the "Tairiku Shimpo" said
yesterday. Another Chinese suspect,
believed to be an accomplice of the
prisoner, escaped, the Japanese daily
reported.

Seized on the person and in the
baggage of the prisoner, the "Tai-
riku Shimpo" stated were instructions
regarding terrorism signed by Gen-
eral Chiang Kai-shek, anti-Japanese
handbills, and "secret documents."
The man was believed to have come
to Shanghai from Chungking to
establish contact with terrorist or-
ganizations located here. He wore
white underwear, which the paper
said—was the uniform of the
"Patriotic and Loyal Society."

The arrest was carried out by
Japanese members of the River
Police, according to the daily.

Interference by a private of the Japanese
Gendarmerie with passengers landing on
No. 1 Pontoon.

Sir,

At 7.45p.m. on July 21st a telephone message
was received at this station from Mr. Sullivan,
Police Sub-Station, No.4 Pontoon, the Bund, to the
effect that the services of a foreign and Japanese
detectives were required by S.I. Biggs at No. 1
Pontoon as a Japanese Gendarmerie was preventing
Chinese passengers to disembark from a boat. D.P.S.
Yoshinaga and the undersigned attended and from
enquiries made it appears that Corp. .V. Eki, of
the Japanese Gendarmerie on duty on No. 1 Pontoon
put up a wooden barrier of the P.W.D. across the
gangway of the pontoon and prevented passengers of
the "S.S. Hsien Kiang" to go ashore.

J.P.C.s 39 and 42 of the River Police, who came
on duty on the pontoon to supervise the landing of the
passengers, then explained to Corp. .V. Eki that the
passengers should be allowed to go ashore and the
barrier then was removed.

D.P.S. Yoshinaga asked Corp. L.V. Eki to explain
the reason for putting up the barrier as stated above,

At 4.10p.m. 5-7-39 a telephone message was
received from Insp. Lees to the effect that the S.S.

disembarking in the usual manner.

berthed at 3.55p.m., and officers attached to the

permission to land until the Japanese had searched the
ship. The Japanese Gendarmes then went on board and
took into custody two male and one female Chinese, names
and other particulars unknown. Sgt. Sergeant Katcham
attached to the Customs River Police attended and
informed D.S.I. Kobayashi that the arrested persons
would first be taken to the River Police Station for
enquiries before being handed over to the Japanese
Gendarmerie.

New River Police Sub-Station
This junk, loaned by the Japanese Navy, has been renovated and converted for use as the new Soochow Creek Sub-station of the Customs River Police. Moored near Honan Road Bridge, the sub-station will be headquarters for personnel engaged in controlling traffic and preventing congestion in Soochow Creek.

River Police Open
New Sub-Station

Headquarters for Control
Of Creek Traffic Posted
Near Honan Road Bridge

In order to exercise more effective control over traffic in Soochow Creek a sub-station of the Customs River Police was yesterday established in Soochow Creek near Honan Road Bridge. This is the first time that a River Police sub-station has been stationed in the creek and it was due to the congestion of the waterway, which is daily becoming worse, that such a move was inaugurated.

The personnel of the new sub-station, consisting of four foreign officers and twenty Chinese under the direction of Sub-Inspector C. Avison, will be charged with the control of traffic on the waterway on the seven-mile stretch between Jessfield Bridge and the Whangpoo River. This duty was taken care of by personnel from the Pootung Point station of the Customs River Police in previous years but the limited number of launches and sampans made the task difficult.

With a new sub-station on the creek proper and with the employment of a launch and sampans for patrol duty a great saving in time will be accomplished. Since the hostilities ended in Shanghai the number of craft using Soochow Creek and the junks lying on both sides of the creek have increased and have become a serious detriment to both the waterway and the trade of the port. It is hoped by the personnel of the new sub-station to better control traffic on the waterway and keep the channel clear.

Japanese Loan Junk
A junk, loaned to the River Police by the Japanese Navy, has been renovated for use as the new sub-station and was towed into position early morning. The vessel has been moored on the North side of the creek, near Honan Road Bridge, the site being chosen because it is in the midst of heavy traffic. With the sub-station located in the most troublesome spot in the creek, congestion in this area will be materially and noticeably relieved. Personnel of the station will be kept in touch with the main creek police station by telephone and radio.

新水上警察分署
这艘由日本海军借出的舢板经过翻新和改造，用作海关水上警察的新苏州河分署。该分署停泊在河南路桥附近，将成为负责控制苏州河交通和防止拥堵的工作人员的总部。

水上警察开设
新分署

控制中心设立
在河南路桥附近
以管理河道交通

为了更有效地控制苏州河的交通，海关水上警察昨日在河南路桥附近的苏州河设立了一个分署。这是首次在水道内设立水上警察分署，此举是由于水道拥堵状况日益严重而发起的。

新分署的人员由四名外籍警官和二十名华籍警员组成，在 C. Avison 副督察的指挥下，将负责杰斯菲尔德桥（Jessfield Bridge，即曹家渡桥）至黄浦江之间七英里航段的水上交通管制。过去，这项任务由海关水上警察浦东角站的人员承担，但由于巡逻艇和舢板数量有限，任务十分困难。

随着在苏州河本体上设立新分署，并启用巡逻艇和舢板执行巡逻任务，将大大节省时间。自上海战事结束以来，使用苏州河的船只数量以及停泊在河道两侧的舢板数量有所增加，已对水道和港口贸易造成严重阻碍。新分署的工作人员希望能更好地控制水上交通，保持航道畅通。

日本借出舢板
一艘由日本海军借给水上警察的舢板经过翻新后用作新分署，并于清晨拖至指定位置。该船停泊在河道北侧，靠近河南路桥，选址原因是该处交通繁忙。由于分署位于苏州河最麻烦的地段，该区域的拥堵状况将得到实质性和显著的缓解。分署人员将通过电话和无线电与主河道警察局保持联系。
